name: Liang Zhaoxian
forbes_bio: Liang Zhaoxian is president of Galanz Group, one of China's largest suppliers of microwave ovens, air conditioners and household appliances.
The company traces its roots to 1978 when it was founded as a feather product plant.
Privately held Galanz is headquartered in the southern Chinese city of Foshan.

name: Sergio Stevanato
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Sergio Stevanato is chairman emeritus of the Stevanato Group, a medical packaging firm based in Piombino Dese, Italy.
Founded by his father Giovanni in 1949, the company is now run by his sons Franco and Marco, who serve as chairman and vice chairman, respectively.
Stevanato Group went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2021.
Stevanato Group is the second largest maker of glass vials in the world and a major supplier of vials for several Covid-19 vaccine manufacturers.
The company started out making glass bottles for wine and perfume and is now one of the world's largest producers of insulin pen cartridges.
forbes_facts: Stevanato owns a winery in northeast Italy, Tenuta Stella, named after the Stevanato Group's original name, Soffieria Stella.
In 2007, Stevanato was appointed a Cavaliere del Lavoro, one of Italy's highest civilian honors.

name: David Zalik
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: David Zalik is the cofounder and former CEO of financial technology company GreenSky, which Goldman Sachs acquired in an all-stock transaction worth about $2.2 billion in 2022.
Goldman sold GreenSky to a consortium of investors in 2024, and Zalik left the company.
The Atlanta-based GreenSky has facilitated billions of dollars in loans for home improvement projects via a network of banks and thousands of contractors.
The business also helps with financing for doctor, dentist and veterinary visits.
Zalik immigrated to the U.S. from Israel at age four when his father, a mathematics professor, got a job at the University of Rhode Island.
forbes_facts: Zalik started his first business at the age of 14, buying computer parts from distributors and assembling them himself.
Zalik didn't attend high school and never graduated from college.

name: Du Sha
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2019-2020); Hurun Global (2014-2021); Hurun China (2001-2021)
forbes_bio: Du Sha is the chairman of Pacific Links International, a global golf club membership group.
Du founded the HomeWorld Group in 1992, and built the company into two major retail chains with 97 superstores before selling them off.
Son Jeff runs a successful investment company in Beijing.

name: Craig McCaw
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Wireless pioneer Craig McCaw and his brothers took over their dad's cable-TV business in 1966.
They sold McCaw Cellular to AT&T in 1994 for $12.6 billion in stock.
McCaw, with backing from Bill Gates and Boeing, cofounded Teledesic in 1990 to provide internet access via satellite. It ceased operations in 2002.
He has stayed out of the limelight since stepping down as chairman of telecom operator Clearwire in 2010, two years before it was acquired by Sprint.
forbes_facts: McCaw owns private James Island off the coast of Vancouver.

name: Wang Wenxue
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2012-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2021); Hurun China (2009-2021)
forbes_bio: Wang Wenxue chairs Shanghai-listed China Fortune Land Development, a large developer of industrial parks in Asia, with 30+ facilities in China alone.
Wang also owns shares in three other China-listed companies: Blackcow Food, Xian Hongsheng Technology and Jiangsu Yulong Steel Pipe.
Wang sold a 20% stake in China Fortune Land to Chinese insurer Ping An for $2 billion in September 2018.

name: Torsten Reil
forbes_bio: Torsten Reil is cofounder and co-CEO of German defense tech company Helsing, which makes AI-powered military drones.
Helsing last raised funds at an $18 billion valuation in July 2026.
Reil started Helsing in 2021 along with cofounders Gundbert Scherf and Niklas Kohler.

name: Zhang Fan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhang Fan is founder and chairman of Shenzhen Goodix Technology, a touch-screen maker.
Goodix clients include Huawei, Lenovo, OPPO, vivo, ZTE, Meizu and Xiaomi.
In 2016 Goodix went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
Zhang is a graduate of the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.
